hook: Search ads catch demand. Social ads create it. Know which one your mission needs.
direction: Education post: Google captures existing intent (people searching "church near me," "counseling in York"); Meta builds awareness for causes nobody knows to search for. Diagram graphic.

facebook.text:
Search ads catch demand. Social ads create it. Know which one your mission needs.

Google Ads work because someone is already looking. When a person types "church near me" or "counseling in York," they have intent. Your ad meets them at the moment they're ready.

Meta Ads work differently. Nobody searches for a cause they've never heard of. Social ads build awareness first — they introduce your ministry, your nonprofit, your business to people who didn't know they needed you.

Neither is better. They solve different problems. The question is which problem you actually have right now.

instagram.text:
Search ads catch demand. Social ads create it. Know which one your mission needs.

Google Ads work because someone is already searching — "church near me," "counseling in York." Intent is there. Your ad just shows up.

Meta Ads work when nobody knows to search for you yet. They build awareness before the need is named.

Different tools. Different jobs. Knowing the difference saves real money.

posts: Google Ads catch people already searching. Meta Ads reach people who don't know you exist yet. One captures demand. One builds it. Wrong choice wastes budget fast.

image.alt: A two-column comparison diagram contrasting Google Ads (captures existing search intent) on the left with Meta Ads (builds awareness for unknown causes) on the right.
